claim_summary: The work supplies a trainable time-series encoder and CoT-supervised LLM adaptation for natural-language reasoning and zero-shot analysis of time-series.

claim_evidence.quote: across various domains with powerful zero-shot performance. First, we train a lightweight time-series encoder on top of an LLM to directly extract time-series information.

modules.name: Time-series encoder and embedding projection
modules.scope_reason: R2 LLM test: the trainable patch encoder and projection change how numerical series reach the LLM embedding space; task changes do not require redesigning temporal state, action space, tool semantics, or a verifier, so the Harness layer tests do not apply.

evidence.quote: We first divide the input time-series into fixed, non-overlapping patches [14] and feed these patches into a multi-head self-attention encoder.
This is then followed by a linear layer which projects the features to match the dimensionality of the LLM’s word embedding.
Stage 1: Encoder warm-up. We train the encoder and projection layer from scratch for next token prediction while keeping the LLM frozen.
